disposition.title: The complete-intersection conjecture for uniform partition systems
disposition.statement:
Let $\mathcal{U}^n_k$ be the family of uniform $k$-partitions of an $n$-set, and let a partition system be **$t$-intersecting** when every two partitions have at least $t$ common classes. For $0\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{k-t}{2}\right\rfloor$, define 
$$
\mathcal{P}_i(n,k,t)=\left\{P\in\mathcal{U}^n_k:\left|P\cap\{[1,c],[c+1,2c],\ldots,[(t+2i-1)c+1,(t+2i)c]\}\right|\geq t+i\right\}.
$$
 

**Complete-intersection conjecture.** For $n\geq k\geq t\geq1$, if $\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{U}^n_k$ is $t$-intersecting, then 
$$
|\mathcal{P}|\leq\max_{0\leq i\leq (k-t)/2}|\mathcal{P}_i(n,k,t)|.
$$
 

The source presents this as the partition-system analogue of the Ahlswede–Khachatrian theorem. It also conjectures uniqueness up to permutations of the ground set; the fuller candidate statement is recorded here as the principal claim.
disposition.source_name: Karen Meagher, “Covering arrays on graphs: qualitative independence graphs and extremal set partition theory”, arXiv:math/0701553 (2007).
disposition.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701553

disposition.title: The infinitude of primes of every odd weight at least 3
disposition.statement: Let $p_n$ denote the $n$th prime, and let its weight be the weight in the paper's decomposition of primes. **Odd-weight prime conjecture.** For every integer $k\ge 3$ that is not a multiple of $2$, the number of primes with weight equal to $k$ is infinite. The claim extends the weight-three formulation of the twin prime conjecture by analogy with the corresponding result for natural numbers; no rigorous argument is given.

disposition.title: The uniform partially-intersecting partition-system conjecture
disposition.statement:
Let $\mathcal{U}^n_k$ be the family of uniform $k$-partitions of an $n$-set. Two partitions are **partially $t$-intersecting** if some class from each has intersection of size at least $t$.

**Uniform partial-intersection conjecture.** Let $k,c,t$ be positive integers with $t\leq c$ and $n=ck$. If $\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{U}^n_k$ is partially $t$-intersecting, then 
$$
|\mathcal{P}|\leq\binom{n-t}{c-t}U(n-c,k-1).
$$
 Moreover, equality holds if and only if, up to a permutation of $[1,n]$, 
$$
\mathcal{P}=\{P\in\mathcal{U}^n_k:[1,t]\subseteq P_i\text{ for some }P_i\in P\}.
$$
 

The conjecture generalizes the preceding partially 2-intersecting problem from arbitrary partition systems to uniform partition systems.
disposition.source_name: Karen Meagher, “Covering arrays on graphs: qualitative independence graphs and extremal set partition theory”, arXiv:math/0701553 (2007).
disposition.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701553

disposition.title: Conjecture on the type of minimum-weight non-codeword minimal pseudo-codewords
disposition.literal_statement:
Let $q$ be even, let $\mathbf{H}=\mathbf{H}_{\operatorname{PG}(2,q)}$, and let the type of a pseudo-codeword be $\boldsymbol{t}=(t_0,t_1,t_2,\ldots)$, where $t_\ell$ counts components of value $\ell$. Consider minimal pseudo-codewords that are not multiples of minimal codewords and have minimal AWGNC pseudo-weight among all such minimal pseudo-codewords.

**Type conjecture.** The type $\boldsymbol{t}$ of these pseudo-codewords has $t_0$ non-negative, $t_1$ positive, $t_2$ positive, and $t_\ell=0$ otherwise. If this is false, the smallest $\tilde\ell$ should instead satisfy $t_\ell\geq0$ for $\ell\in\{0,1,\ldots,\tilde\ell\}$ and $t_\ell=0$ otherwise.

A positive answer would improve understanding of minimal pseudo-codewords and, in particular, the AWGNC pseudo-weight spectrum gap. The supplied text gives no resolution of this conjecture.

disposition.title: The Genocchi descent pattern conjecture for packed words
disposition.statement:
Let $I$ and $J$ be compositions of $n$, and let $W”(I,J)$ be the set of packed words $w$ such that

$$
\operatorname{GC}(\operatorname{Std}(w))=I \qquad\text{and}\qquad \operatorname{ev}(w)=J.
$$

Here $\operatorname{totg}(w)$ denotes the number of occurrences of the patterns $21$-$1$ and $31$-$2$ in $w$. **The Genocchi descent pattern conjecture.**

$$
E_I^J(q)=\sum_{w\in W”(I,J)}q^{\operatorname{totg}(w)}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a pattern-counting interpretation of the generating function $E_I^J(q)$, whose specialization at $q=1$ counts packed words with the prescribed Genocchi composition and evaluation. The paper presents preliminary examples but does not establish the $q$-enumeration in general.
disposition.source_name: Jean-Christophe Novelli, Jean-Yves Thibon and Lauren K. Williams, “Combinatorial Hopf algebras, noncommutative Hall-Littlewood functions, and permutation tableaux”, arXiv:0804.0995 (2009).
disposition.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.0995

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2008).

disposition.title: The projective space derangement graph conjecture for PGL(n+1,q)
disposition.statement: Let $\mathbb{P}_q^n$ be projective $n$-space, with $n\geq 1$, and let $\Gamma_{\operatorname{PGL}(n+1,q)}$ be the derangement graph of $\operatorname{PGL}(n+1,q)$ acting on $\mathbb{P}_q^n$. An independent set is a set of vertices containing no adjacent pair, and a coset of the stabilizer of a point or hyperplane is a left or right coset of the corresponding setwise stabilizer. **The projective space derangement graph conjecture.** Any independent set of maximal size in $\Gamma_{\operatorname{PGL}(n+1,q)}$ is either the coset of the stabilizer of a point or the coset of the stabilizer of a hyperplane. The source notes that both types attain the maximal size, while for $n\geq 2$ they are not conjugate; no classification beyond these examples is given.

disposition.title: The generalized Bunkbed conjecture for two-color edge percolation
disposition.literal_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph, let $T\subseteq V(G)$, and let $\tilde G=G\times K_2$. In the model $E_3^T(\tilde G)$, every horizontal edge is assigned independently to the downstairs or upstairs layer with equal probability, and vertical edges are present exactly at vertices in $T$. Equivalently, color every edge of $G$ red or blue independently with equal probability; a walk may change color only at a vertex of $T$.

**Two-color Bunkbed conjecture.** For every $u,v\in V(G)$,

$$
P(u_0\longleftrightarrow v_0)\ge P(u_0\longleftrightarrow v_1).
$$

This is a stronger-looking reformulation of the conditioned model and is proved in the paper for some graph classes. Its validity for arbitrary graphs and arbitrary $T$ remains open.
disposition.reason: Exact finite two-color conditioned E3 model, not independent horizontal percolation. A swap-colors bijection changes the starting layer too and does not compare required same-start events. Modern bunkbed counterexamples are a prior-art alert; no model-transfer proof or small exact witness established here.

disposition.title: The core conjecture for qualitative independence graphs
disposition.statement:
A graph is a **core** if every endomorphism is an automorphism. Let $QI(k^2,k)$ be the qualitative independence graph.

**Core conjecture.** For any positive integer $k$, the graph $QI(k^2,k)$ is a core.

The case $k=3$, namely $QI(9,3)$, is known by work cited in the paper. The conjecture asks for the analogous rigidity for all $k$.

disposition.title: Conjecture on unions of intersecting strictly informative groves
disposition.statement:
Let two groves be **strictly informative** if each satisfies the strict informativeness criterion for determining supertrees. Let the groves be collections of taxon sets, with intersection and union taken as collections of taxon sets. **Strictly informative grove union conjecture.** The union of two intersecting strictly informative groves is a grove.

This is proposed as a weaker statement related to the earlier conjecture on groves. The paper gives a counterexample showing that the union of two intersecting strictly informative groves need not itself be strictly informative, even when it is a grove; the conjecture asserts only the weaker grove property.

disposition.primary_scope: A topology assignment may depend on the partition. A grove requires either no cross triple or some informative compatible rooted-tree assignment for EVERY nontrivial partition. Strictly informative requires the latter for every such partition. Intersection is as collections of taxon sets.
disposition.mathematical_attempt: Enumerated all rooted binary supertrees on 4,5,6 taxa and projected them to input taxon sets. Compatible assignments are restriction-signature classes. A cross triple is resolved iff its rooted resolution is constant in such a class. Exhaustive family classifications and union tests are in logs/groves.log. Mixed 3/4-element taxon sets on six taxa gave 1100 strictly informative families of size 2..4 after a necessary private-taxon filter; 5000 sampled intersecting pairs passed. Seven-taxon bitset computation used all 10395 rooted binary trees, classified 3000 sampled private-taxon families, found 1277 distinct strict families and tested 1000 intersecting pairs without a witness. Full six-taxon all-pairs extension hit the wall cap and is NOT credited as complete.
disposition.remaining_gap: No general union lemma or counterexample. Need control of resolved triples when a partition of the union masks cross triples of either constituent. Small family tests cannot supply that bridge. The source Remark 3.19 example itself fails the stated strict criterion in our diagnostic; it is an adjacent source defect, not a solution of Conjecture 3.13.

disposition.title: The hypergraph Bunkbed conjecture
disposition.literal_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph, let $T\subseteq V(G)$, and let $\mathcal U=\{U_1,\ldots,U_k\}$ be a partition of $E$ into connected subgraphs. In the model $E_4^{T,\mathcal U}(G)$, all edges in each $U_i$ receive the same color, red or blue, independently and with equal probability; a walk may change color only at a vertex in $T$.

**Hypergraph Bunkbed conjecture.** For every $u,v\in V(G)$,

$$
P(u_0\longleftrightarrow v_0)\ge P(u_0\longleftrightarrow v_1).
$$

This generalizes the two-color model by allowing connected groups of edges to share a color, and is needed for the paper's outerplanar-graph argument. The assertion is not established in general.
